summary: Explored the depth/width and LR/schedule/batch-size space under the fixed 5-minute budget across 36 runs. The dominant lever was TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE: shrinking it from the baseline 2^19 tokens/step to ~163840 (more, noisier optimizer steps per wallclock second) gave the single biggest gain. On top of that, lowering WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1 and adding a small LR warmup (~3% of budget) each gave further small but consistent gains, and once those were retuned the optimal DEPTH shifted down from 10 to 9, landing at val_bpb=0.979324 (reconfirmed twice at 0.979623 and via a WARMDOWN_RATIO ablation at 0.980533 for the untested variant). Perturbing MATRIX_LR, EMBEDDING_LR, ADAM_BETAS, and WARMDOWN_RATIO around their defaults did not help and mostly fell within noise (~0.001-0.002 bpb). Depth alone (holding original hyperparameters fixed) was a weaker, non-monotonic lever, and very deep models (14+) ran out of steps or OOM'd in 5 minutes. Next things worth trying: joint/coarse grid search over (depth, batch size, weight decay) rather than one-variable-at-a-time since these hyperparameters interact; also untried architecture levers like ASPECT_RATIO, HEAD_DIM, and WINDOW_PATTERN.
